body.jsonRpcTitle: Add a JSON-RPC 2.0 call with the next free id. A second call turns the body into a batch.
body.formatTitle: Indent the {{type}} body ({{chord}}). {{example}} are kept as written.
body.cannotFormatAt: The {{type}} cannot be formatted at line {{line}}, column {{column}}: {{message}}
body.noBodyDescription: This request is sent without a body.
body.natsSocket: A NATS request sends the body to the subject in the address and shows the first reply. Add ?mode=publish to send without waiting for a reply, or ?mode=subscribe to wait for the first message on the subject. Put a token or user:password before the host. Only the desktop app sends them.
body.rawSocket: TCP and UDP requests send the body as bytes: text as written, or hex digits such as 48 65 6c 6c 6f. The reply is read until the server closes the connection or the timeout passes; UDP waits for one datagram. Only the desktop app sends them.
body.multipartOnGet: GET requests rarely carry a body, and many servers ignore it. Switch the method to POST or PUT if this should be uploaded.
body.replacedByGraphQL: The method is GRAPHQL, so the body is built from the GraphQL tab and this one is not sent.

encoder.title: Encode JSON as a binary format
encoder.description: Writes the JSON below as MessagePack or CBOR and attaches the result as the file body. The JSON is encoded now, so {{variables}} are not replaced when the request is sent.
encoder.failed: The JSON could not be encoded: {{message}}
